t: The Apache speak languages of the Athabaskan family, related to that of the Navajo, and came into the Southwest from the north several centuries before the Spanish arrived.
Each Apache tribe is politically autonomous; historically the six major groups were independent of one another and sometimes fought each other.
After centuries of war with Spain, Mexico and the United States, and forced removals onto reservations, the Apache population has rebounded to 148,936 in the 2020 census.
dyk: Before the reservations, Apache families were mostly matrilocal: a married daughter's new dwelling was built near her mother's, and her husband joined her family, while among the Chiricahua a man avoided even the sight of his wife's female relatives.
ev: Francisco Coronado meets bison-hunting 'Querechos', possibly Plains Apaches, on the plains east of the Pueblos
Juan de Oñate makes the first known written record of the name Apache
The first Apache raids on Sonora appear to take place
Juan José Compà is killed for Mexican bounty money, and Mangas Coloradas becomes principal chief
The US Army forces about 1,500 Yavapai and Tonto Apache on a winter march to San Carlos that kills several hundred
An uprising against the reservation system begins Victorio's War
Geronimo's band surrenders at Skeleton Canyon and is sent to military confinement in Florida

f.homeland: Apacheria: the mountains, valleys, canyons, deserts and southern Great Plains of what is now eastern Arizona, New Mexico, West Texas, southern Colorado and Sonora and Chihuahua; today tribes and reservations in Arizona, New Mexico, Texas and Oklahoma, among them Fort Apache, San Carlos, Mescalero and Jicarilla, and communities in Sonora, Chihuahua, Coahuila and Tamaulipas
f.period: migration from the Athabascan homelands of the north into the Southwest between 1000 and 1500 CE (the history gives AD 1200 to 1500); first Spanish written record in 1598; raids on Sonora from the late 17th century; wars with Mexico and the United States in the 19th century; reservations from the 1870s; Geronimo's surrender in 1886
f.known: six major groups: Chiricahua, Jicarilla, Lipan, Mescalero, Plains and Western Apache; wickiups and tipis; agave (mescal) as a staple food; the Sunrise Dance puberty ceremony of young women; the culture heroes Killer-Of-Enemies and Child-Of-The-Water; long resistance under leaders such as Mangas Coloradas, Victorio and Geronimo
f.sources: Spanish accounts from Coronado in 1541 and Juan de Oñate in 1598; church baptism records studied by David M. Brugge; anthropologists such as Morris Opler, Grenville Goodwin and Keith Basso, working with Apache informants; archaeology of the Dismal River culture and the Cerro Rojo complex; linguistics from Harry Hoijer onward; census and Indian Affairs figures
